newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar drifts in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar drifts in light trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar drifted all day Monday, closing at C$1.3702 (US$0.7299) from Friday's close of C$1.3701 (US$0.7299).
* The currency was range-bound on decreasing expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would soon increase interest rates, dealers said.
* The currency is expected to firm on export data this week.

On Friday a report showed consumer prices in the United States rose 0.1 percent in August compared with expectations of a 0.2 percent rise. The numbers have diminished expectations that rates will rise.
The Canadian currency will likely stay range-bound until fresh data is released on Tuesday and Wednesday, said Gregory.
Canadian manufacturing numbers are expected on Tuesday and merchandise trade will be released Wednesday.
The numbers will likely highlight Canada's strong export sector and perhaps give the currency a boost, Gregory said.
"It could be a spark for the Canada dollar," he said.
"There's nothing like good trade numbers to get a currency all excited."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar softened to 1.1015 marks from Friday's close of 1.1044 marks, and softened to 80.29 yen from 80.60 yen.
